name: Harness, context, sub-agents and recursion ranked
purpose: Harnesses are ranked by cost and time at the same pass rate, across the context given to them and their use of sub-agents and recursion.
record: A balanced score of pass rate, cost and time for each setting, on the same cases. The cases that can tell depth from none are the depth set, evaluation/agent_sessions_depth (balanced by [balance.agent_sessions_depth] in esoi.toml, the same weights as the other sets): five public synthetic cases, each scored by code with no model judge. A multi-part task over five separable sites, where each part needs its own reading and facts are checked per part; a folder that carries solution records (a parent delegating to three children, each with a milestone, and a retired one), checked by hidden tests per child; a fact held only in a skills folder outside the work folder, handed as case data to an arm whose constructor takes skills_dir; an earlier finding handed as case data to an arm whose constructor takes recall, with a planted wrong claim in the folder that must be verified and rejected; and a small one-file fix where sub-agents are waste, which scores the same whatever is used and shows the overuse as cost, time and the sub-agent calls the row records. An arm whose constructor takes neither input gets the goal and the folder alone, so an arm without skills or recall can lose where it could not on the hard set.
disadvantages: Five cases cannot separate close arms: repeat the set at least three times per arm and pool; the skills case could in principle be solved by an arm that searches the machine for the skills folder; sub-agent calls and turns are recorded only for runs whose result exposes them; the cases are synthetic and small beside real deep work.

name: Open-ended work finished per cost and time (agent sessions)
purpose: An arm (an agent harness, the provider it drives and a tier) is ranked by how much open-ended work it finishes correctly, for what it costs and how long it takes, on the same cases as every other arm.
record: The balanced score of [balance.agent_sessions] in esoi.toml (pass rate, cost per case and seconds per case, with the weights and budgets stated there), per arm, over evaluation/agent_sessions: read-and-report tasks, coding tasks checked by their own tests (restored by the harness before the check) and milestone-shaped deliverables checked by a written rubric (a video script, research that cites its source files, a dated plan from notes). Every run is recorded, partial ones included, with calls, cost and seconds. A harness is ranked against another only on results with the same model (harness_ranking); a pair with no model in common is listed as not compared, with the run that would settle it, and is never counted as beaten.
disadvantages: Eighteen cases written by one author cannot separate close arms; the deliverables are judged by rubric terms, not by how well they read; the research case uses local sources, not the live web; Claude Code dollars are the CLI's list-price estimate on a flat subscription; public problems may be known to the model.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new arm (harness, provider, tier) is described: its five ratings and reasons are a row of arm_ideas.csv beside the solution, rated before it is built] > offline [real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the harness's own tests pass with no model: test_headless_runner.py replays each harness's recorded event stream through a fake program (report, tokens, cost, launch failure, time limit, cancel, escalation), and the Claude Code runner tests pass; the none arm is the zero bound] > public [real=no | when=the arm has an unexpired prior of grade C or better in public_priors.csv beside the solution, set by the prior rule of docs/explanation/public-evidence.md (direct or borrowed from a published live-benchmark row, never estimated); a prior orders unmeasured arms and never outranks a measured result] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=the offline stage passed for the harness and the arm's provider has credentials where we measure: one real case runs end to end and its report is read by hand] > staged [sample=sample:6 | real=yes | gate=competitive | max-age-days=90 | when=the one case passed and a call budget is set with --max-calls: two cases of each kind] > whole [sample=full | real=yes | min-pass-rate=0.94 | max-age-days=90 | when=the staged sample passed its gate, or did not separate the leading arms; the min-pass-rate is the floor an arm must hold here before the hard set counts for it]

name: Hard deep work finished per cost and time (agent sessions)
purpose: An arm (harness, provider, tier, and any instructions pack) is ranked by how much real deep work it finishes correctly, for its cost and time: work that takes minutes and fails on a weak tier.
record: The balanced score of [balance.agent_sessions_hard] in esoi.toml (accuracy 95 percent, cost and time 2.5 each, so one more passed case outweighs everything cost and time can add) over evaluation/agent_sessions_hard; the metric alone selects, by selection_stages.py: the open-ended whole stage at its floor, the hard whole stage at its floor (the coding cases all pass), at least three counting hard runs (skipped while no arm has them), the depth stage (evaluation/agent_sessions_depth, five code-scored cases that need parts read separately, records in the folder, skills outside it, an earlier finding or no depth at all; its floor is four of five pooled over at least three runs, a stage that skips while no arm has the runs, and cost per case decides among arms within noise of each other on the depth set too), a recorded real task when any arm has one, then the highest pooled hard pass rate, with cost and then time deciding only among arms not significantly or by a whole case per run lower; an arm that needs a credential the install lacks is not selectable on that install; multi-file coding changes modelled on real deep tasks, checked by the tests the agent sees and hidden tests written to the rules the goal states, and milestone deliverables over the real records a milestone turn read, each rubric item judged by the strongest Anthropic tier with a quote that must be in the evidence. The case bodies are private; the repository holds their ids and digests. A harness is ranked against another only on results with the same model (harness_ranking); a pair with no model in common is listed as not compared, with the run that would settle it, and is never counted as beaten.
disadvantages: Seven cases cannot separate close arms; the deliverable judge is a Claude model judging Claude arms; the coding cases are rebuilt packages, not the real repositories; the judge's time is inside each case's seconds, the same for every arm. The judged deliverables pass or fail differently from run to run on the same arm, so one run of the set does not rank two harnesses on ability: repeat the deliverable cases many times per arm before claiming a difference (the changelog records the repeated comparison of the hub's own loop with Claude Code). The deliverable whose notes set a limit in one file and the amount used in another fails most runs for every harness on the fast tier.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new arm or instructions pack is described: rated in arm_ideas.csv] > offline [real=no | gate=all-pass | when=each coding case fails as given and passes with a reference fix (checked when the private cases are built), and the runner tests pass] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=the arm passed the whole stage of metric-delegated-agent-sessions: one hard case, hand-read] > whole [sample=full | real=yes | min-pass-rate=0.66 | max-age-days=90 | when=the one case passed, or it failed on a tier whose stronger rung is being measured: every hard case; the six coding cases must pass, the three judged deliverables are decided by repeated runs]

name: A run finds what it needs instead of asking
purpose: A run that is not handed a fact the work needs finds it by a route a competent colleague would use (a file's history, a database file, a command's output, the web) and does not ask the person, who cannot answer.
record: Free stage: for each arm, which routes its own tool surface can reach (files, history by script or git, a database file, command output, web search, a page fetch, a service by script), read from its configuration. Paid stage: the long cases of evaluation/agent_sessions_hard in which the one missing fact is only discoverable (a revision history file, an audit table in the database) and a hidden test checks the real value, so asking, inventing or skipping it fails the case.
disadvantages: Two long cases, synthetic, written by one author; the free stage reads the surface and not the behaviour; a run may find the fact by luck; a fact behind a service that needs credentials is not covered.
cascading_conditionals: free [real=no | gate=all-pass | when=hubofhubs/the_world/tools/delegated_agent_sessions/tests/test_resourcefulness_surface.py passes] > paid [real=yes | gate=competitive | when=the long hard cases are in the private case folder and the spend is approved]
